mainTopic: Does רב follow אומדנא (judging by a person's likely intent)? The case of a שכיב מרע's gift that was also made with a קנין.
overview: This amud opens with the last item in a list of rulings where the הלכה follows a certain view: the case of תרומת מעשר taken from דמאי. The גמרא then challenges the earlier assumption that רב does not go by אומדנא, meaning judging by a person's likely intent. To build the challenge, it quotes a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a deathbed gift that was also made with a קנין. בי רב say the giver 'made him ride on two horses.' The gift is like a healthy person's gift, so the giver cannot take it back if he recovers. It is also like a deathbed gift, so a loan owed to him passes on by words alone. שמואל says he does not know how to rule. Perhaps the extra קנין shows the giver wanted the transfer done by a שטר, and a שטר cannot take effect after death.

steps.title: The last case in the list: separating from doubtfully tithed produce
steps.stepSummary: The list of cases where the הלכה follows this view ends with תרומת מעשר של דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה also follows his view about תרומת מעשר taken from דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the earlier discussion. It adds one more case where the הלכה follows this view: תרומת מעשר taken from דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' at the start tells us this is the end of a list that began before this section. The new item is a case about produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion a לוי must give to a כהן from the מעשר he receives
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, which may or may not have been tithed

phrases.english: And with regard to the teruma of the tithe of demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a list of rulings from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows this view also in the case of תרומת מעשר of דמאי.

steps.title: Challenge: does רב really ignore a person's likely intent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב truly does not go by אומדנא. It brings a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a deathbed gift that was also made with a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really not follow אומדנא? But it was taught: about a deathbed gift whose document says a קנין was made, the school of רב said in רב's name: 'He made him ride on two horses.' And שמואל said: 'I do not know what to rule about it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier idea that רב does not judge by a person's likely intent. To set up the challenge, it quotes a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a deathbed gift made with a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שכיב מרע can give a gift without a קנין, so making a קנין is extra. The question is how to treat a gift that has both. רב's school says it gets the strength of both kinds of gift. שמואל is unsure. The גמרא will build its challenge on רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An estimate of what a person most likely meant
A gift given by a person on his deathbed
A formal act that transfers ownership
'He made him ride on two horses': the gift gets two kinds of strength

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'does רב not follow אומדנא?' is not a simple request for information. It is a challenge: the גמרא is about to show that רב's own ruling seems to depend on a person's likely intent.

phrases.english: And does Rav not follow assessment of intent?
But it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: A deathbed gift in which an act of acquisition is written,
in the school of Rav they say in Rav's name:
He made him ride on two horses.
And Shmuel said:
I do not know what to rule about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב לָא אָזֵיל בָּתַר אוּמְדָּנָא? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the list of rulings to question the earlier assumption about רב's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier assumption that רב does not go by אומדנא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own ruling about a deathbed gift made with a קנין seems to depend on guessing the giver's intent.

steps.title: Explaining 'two horses': like both a healthy person's gift and a deathbed gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רב's words in order to explain them: the gift is treated both like a healthy person's gift and like a deathbed gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in רב's name, 'He made him ride on two horses': it is like a healthy person's gift, and it is like a deathbed gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב's phrase again so that it can explain what 'two horses' means. This sets up the specific details in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two 'horses' are two kinds of legal strength. Because of the קנין, the gift is like a healthy person's gift. Because the giver was dying, it is also like a deathbed gift. The receiver gets the benefits of both.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift given by a healthy person

phrases.english: In the school of Rav they say in Rav's name,
he made him ride on two horses:
it is like the gift of a healthy person,
and it is like the gift of a person on his deathbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּבֵי רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמְרִי, אַרְכְּבֵיהּ אַתְּרֵי רִכְשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רב's phrase from the previous step in order to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deathbed gift made with a קנין is treated both as a healthy person's gift and as a deathbed gift.

steps.title: The two benefits: the giver cannot retract, and a loan transfers by words
steps.stepSummary: Like a healthy person's gift, the giver cannot take it back if he recovers. Like a deathbed gift, a loan owed to him can be passed on just by saying so.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a healthy person's gift: if he gets up from his illness, he cannot take it back. It is like a deathbed gift: if he said 'my loan goes to so-and-so,' his loan goes to that person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two 'horses.' It lists one benefit that comes from each kind of gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain deathbed gift is cancelled if the giver recovers. Here the קנין makes it final, like a healthy person's gift. A loan normally cannot be passed on by words alone. Here it can, because the gift is also a deathbed gift.

keyTerms.meaning: He got up, meaning he recovered from his illness
To take back or cancel his gift
My loan, meaning money that someone owes me

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a deathbed gift made with a קנין gets the strengths of both kinds of gift. It stays final even if the giver recovers, and a debt owed to him can be transferred just by speaking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation of רב's view is the material the גמרא will use for its challenge about whether רב follows אומדנא.

phrases.english: It is like the gift of a healthy person,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם עָמַד — אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר בּוֹ.
phrases.english: in that if he arose, he cannot retract it.
phrases.notes: 'Arose' means he got better. A plain deathbed gift would be cancelled then, but the קנין makes this one final.

phrases.english: It is like the gift of a person on his deathbed,
in that if he said, 'My loan is to so-and-so,'
phrases.notes: He means money someone else owes him. Normally that cannot be handed over by words alone.

phrases.english: his loan goes to so-and-so.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא, דְּאִם עָמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two benefits named in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the קנין, the giver cannot retract if he recovers. Because it is a deathbed gift, a loan can be transferred by words alone.

steps.title: שמואל: Maybe the giver wanted a document, and a document cannot work after death
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he does not know how to rule. Maybe the sick man meant the gift to go through only with a שטר, and a שטר cannot take effect once the giver has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: I do not know what to decide about this case. Perhaps the giver only made up his mind to transfer the gift through a document. A document does not work after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the מחלוקת. שמואל, unlike רב, worries that the gift may not work at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain deathbed gift works just by speaking, so the extra קנין looks unnecessary. שמואל suggests the extra קנין shows the giver's real plan: he wanted the transfer to happen in a formal way, by document. A שטר only works while the owner is alive, so once he dies it is too late, and the gift may fail.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know. שמואל is admitting he is unsure how to rule.
He made up his mind to transfer it. This is about the giver's final intention.
A written document, here one that transfers ownership.
A document cannot take effect after the owner's death.

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying deathbed gifts never work. He is unsure only about this special case where the giver added a קנין, because the קנין might reveal that the giver wanted a document.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's reasoning depends on guessing what the giver really intended (אומדנא). This מחלוקת is the source the גמרא brought in step 2 for its challenge about whether רב goes by אומדנא.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
I do not know what to rule about it,
perhaps he did not make up his mind to transfer it
except through a document,
and there is no document after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: לָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי אֵידוּן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's opposing side of the מחלוקת whose רב side was explained in steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל is unsure the gift works. The קנין may show the giver intended a transfer by document, and a document cannot take effect after death.
